claims.wording: The vendor describes a scan, review, then clean workflow with checkboxes; some categories preselect items.
claims.excerpt: every scan lists items with their size and a checkbox; safe categories pre-select for you, risky ones (your files, your apps) stay unchecked until you choose.
claims.conditions: Do not adopt 'safe' as an independent finding or imply nothing is preselected.
claims.location: workflow review checklist and approval row

claims.wording: The documented Space Lens is an exploration-only, folder-by-folder size view.
claims.excerpt: Pure exploration - nothing here is deletable

claims.wording: System Junk is documented to group user/browser/developer caches, logs and crash reports; the page names DerivedData and build caches.
claims.excerpt:
System Junk
- user caches, logs, crash reports, developer-tool caches, and per-browser caches
claims.conditions: Exact adapters, versions, paths and rebuild costs not verified. Reject universal 'all safe to remove' marketing.

claims.wording: Large & Old Files is documented to list files at least 100 MB in Downloads, Documents, Movies and Desktop, largest first.
claims.excerpt: finds big files (≥ 100 MB) scattered across your personal folders - Downloads, Documents, Movies, Desktop - sorted largest first
claims.conditions: Vendor does not define MB units here; large is not disposable.

claims.wording: The vendor lists an Uninstaller, mail attachment cache cleanup, Trash review and startup-extension review.
claims.excerpt:
Uninstaller
- every installed app sorted by disk usage
claims.conditions: Does not prove complete app-residue removal or successful uninstall; each additional category is documented in S1 Highlights.

claims.wording: The documented clean step uses Trash for items the vendor calls safe, with confirmation for permanent deletes.
claims.excerpt: Safe items go to the Trash (reversible); permanent deletes always ask first.
claims.conditions: Not a recovery guarantee or measurement of newly free disk space; no cleanup executed.

claims.wording: DripCleaner is advertised at US$19.99 once for one device; membership Solo Cup US$3.99/month for one device or US$1.99/month paid annually; Family Roast US$7.99/month for up to five devices or US$3.99/month paid annually.
claims.excerpt: Solo Cup ($3.99/month, 1 device) and Family Roast ($7.99/month, up to 5 devices), or $1.99 and $3.99 a month paid annually
claims.conditions: All menu apps included. Annual rates are monthly equivalents, not a monthly-billed $1.99 plan. Annual totals/checkout not independently verified. Taxes and currency conversion may apply. Do not promise lifetime updates.

claims.wording: Activation is documented to require getapps.cafe sign-in; the subscription licence is personal, non-transferable and revocable, dependent on an active subscription. A seven-day membership trial requires a payment method and converts automatically unless cancelled.
claims.excerpt: Starting a trial requires a valid payment method, and the trial converts into a paid subscription automatically
claims.conditions: Sign-in excerpt in S1: 'open it, and sign in once with your getapps.cafe account.' No signup, trial or purchase tested. One-off entitlement terms beyond one-device offer remain unclear.

claims.wording: Minimum macOS, Apple Silicon/Intel coverage, signing/notarization, extra runtimes, fully offline operation, telemetry, helper grouping and recurring-growth monitoring are not verified.
claims.excerpt:
Guided first run
- a short intro walks you through what the app does and helps you grant the one permission it needs
claims.conditions: Permission identity not specified in retained copy. Missing documentation is not proof of feature absence.

claims.wording: No evidence supports measured cleanup savings, speed, blanket safety or guaranteed unrecoverable shredding in this packet.
claims.excerpt: DripCleaner overwrites it with zeros before deleting, so it can't be recovered
claims.conditions: Retained to flag an unverified vendor guarantee, not for endorsement or a shredding tutorial. No destructive tests permitted.

claims.wording: Breathing Room, which we build, is a free Apache-2.0 macOS 13+ preview with optional advertised AI Care at US$5/month or US$50/year.
claims.excerpt: Breathing Room is a free, Apache-2.0 macOS maintenance preview
claims.conditions: capabilities.md pricing and installation tables: 0.1.0-preview.1; universal installer advertised, physical Intel untested; Apple Development signed, not Developer ID/notarized; Python 3.10+ prerequisite. Source implementations are not binary parity certification.

claims.wording: Breathing Room local inspection differs from its authenticated hosted AI; source supports grouped processes, activity history and exact saved daily-care approvals while the app stays running.
claims.excerpt: Hosted AI assistance requires internet access and authentication; this is not an entirely offline AI product.
claims.conditions: capabilities.md source matrix and boundary sections. Relevant paths/process/storage outputs may reach service. Optional narrowly verified Ruff automatic mode prevents unconditional 'never acts without asking' language. No native tests or measured results in this job.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs DripCleaner: cleanup review or ongoing investigation
comparison.intent: Concise Mac purchase/workflow decision, not a repeat of the scan-review article.
comparison.lead: DripCleaner documents category-based cleanup and a one-device purchase option; Breathing Room, which we build, is a maintenance preview with local inspection and optional hosted AI. Neither source packet proves a speed or safety winner.
comparison.visualRequirement: Cleared real competitor app screenshot plus current-source labeled Breathing Room view; neither logos nor link-only visual satisfies the gate.

competitorAdvantages: Documented one-device one-off offer for readers avoiding a recurring app subscription (D09; not a lifetime-update promise).
Documented category-based scan review, exploration-only Space Lens and listed uninstaller (D03–D07), useful for a deliberate periodic tidy.
competitorTradeoffs: Activation requires an account; membership is recurring and trial needs payment method (D10).
Minimum OS, Mac architectures, notarization and monitoring coverage remain not verified; not negative feature claims (D11).
Safety, unrecoverable shredding and headline savings are not independently established (D12).
decisionGuidance.breathingRoomFit: If the task is recurring space-growth investigation with app/helper context, source implements activity/process views and optional hosted assistance (B02); keep preview, Python, authentication/data-sharing and runtime caveats visible.
decisionGuidance.breathingRoomTradeoffs: Non-notarized preview; untested physical Intel/clean-machine behavior; Python 3.10+; optional AI needs account/internet and advertised payment; no certified binary parity or measured savings (B01–B02).
avoid: No unsupported 'best', safer/faster or savings claims.
No all-offline or no-tracking assertions from directory tags.
No Breathing Room Windows support implied by competitor downloads.
No guarantee that every cache is disposable or zero overwrite ensures recovery prevention.
